name: Herbert Hoover
role: 31st US president (1929–1933); Secretary of Commerce (1921–1928); relief administrator
summary: Republican president and former engineer who described his outlook as American individualism: equality of opportunity, voluntary cooperation, regulation to prevent domination, and a refusal to put government into commercial business. He backed protective tariffs and immigration limits, signed the Smoot-Hawley tariff and founded the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, and after 1933 attacked the New Deal as regimentation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hoover negotiated fleet limits that maintained an American navy at parity with the strongest foreign fleet.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hoover signed legislation enlarging the lending powers of the Federal Reserve Banks during the banking crisis.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Praised the founders for not granting hereditary titles and landed estates and said children must not inherit power by right of birth.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Hoover approved the 1932 Revenue Act, retaining and increasing graduated federal taxes on individual income.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hoover called for stronger federal investigative and enforcement capabilities as part of his 1930 law enforcement program.

arms-reduction.rationale: Hoover negotiated and brought into force the London Naval Treaty, which limited fleet strength and reduced warship construction.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: Hoover told the American Federation of Labor that most people displaced by labor-saving devices had found work in new industries and services. He expected continued innovation and improvements in living standards to keep absorbing displaced workers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: With the federal budget already in deficit, Hoover signed a relief and construction measure extending Treasury-financed public credit to accelerate public works and employment.

ban-cartels.rationale: Hoover told Congress that the Sherman Act should remain in force and called prevention of monopoly essential to consumer protection and competition.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Held that the system evolves within itself and that depressions are transitory from which the nation emerges stronger.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Praised the economic individualism that drove invention, production and living standards, though he rejected the label capitalism.

central-planning.rationale: Rejected government direction of production and distribution and called nationalization the negation of American individualism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hoover brought employers and organized labor together at the beginning of the Depression to seek commitments against wage cuts and strikes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wrote that rising standards of living, including non-essentials, need no apology and are the base of civilization.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Hoover credited industrial knowledge, inventions and improved production with raising American living standards in American Individualism.

decide-locally.rationale: Said the American system rests on decentralized local responsibility, limited federal regulation to cases where states lack power, and treated education as primarily a state and local matter.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Named the dictatorship of the proletariat among catchwords that clothe hatred and destruction and called the Russian system a tyranny.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Treated autocracy by birth or divine right as the opposite of American individualism. (Moved from monarchy-legitimate, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about ceremonial heads of state.)

economic-freedom.rationale: In The Challenge to Liberty, Hoover defined liberalism as recognizing that political freedom depends on preserving economic freedom.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Wrote that Americans do not pretend that all people are equal in ability and that government can assure only liberty, justice and equality of opportunity.

farm-price-support.rationale: Hoover signed the Agricultural Marketing Act, which created the Federal Farm Board and authorized financing for stabilization corporations dealing with agricultural surpluses.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Hoover began withdrawing the U.S. administration and Marines from Haiti and drew down the force in Nicaragua, which he retained temporarily at the request of Nicaragua’s government.

free-trade.rationale: Hoover approved the Tariff Act of 1930, imposing protective import duties across a broad range of products.

gradual-change.rationale: Hoover called for reform through the organic development of American institutions and opposed using revolution to solve domestic problems.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Celebrated the gains in living standards, invention and production from industrial development.

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Hoover recommended making the municipality, county or other local unit the organizing base for the public health system.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued that government is practically incompetent at running commercial business, citing the post-war railways, and that business progress depends on competition.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Hoover kept Marines in Nicaragua at the request of its government to help maintain order there while preparing for withdrawal.

military-superiority.rationale: Hoover secured ratification of a naval settlement that reduced shipbuilding competition and established parity with the strongest foreign fleet.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Hoover expanded Federal Reserve authority in 1932 to preserve the gold standard while supplying credit during heavy withdrawals.

national-self-determination.rationale: Hoover objected to the peace treaty’s transfer of large German, Hungarian and Russian populations to new states, arguing that imposing those borders would fuel another war.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said American individualism is not capitalism, socialism or a cross of them, while praising its economic results; mixed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hoover signed federal legislation financing state relief and public construction and created a public corporation to extend emergency credit.

no-bailouts.rationale: Hoover signed the law creating the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, which authorized emergency loans to banks, insurers and railroads in distress.

no-central-bank.rationale: Hoover signed the 1932 law extending the Federal Reserve Banks’ emergency credit powers and the types of assets they could use to issue notes.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Said the system crumbles if citizens choose which laws to support; dislike of a law gives a duty to discourage violation and a right to work for repeal.

party-controls-media.rationale: Argued that expanded government business leads to control of press and platform and that free speech does not outlive free industry.

person-over-state.rationale: Hoover treated individual development as the point of his system and argued that the regimentation of daily life gives government control over people’s thoughts and purposes.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said liberation from widespread poverty gave a higher degree of individual freedom and made equality of opportunity the core of American individualism.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: In his memorandum to Wilson during the Paris peace talks, Hoover argued that securing democracy in Germany should be a paramount objective of the postwar settlement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wrote that private property is not a fetish in America, citing the uncompensated end of the liquor trade, and treated property as an instrument for initiative rather than an end.

public-ownership.rationale: Hoover vetoed the Muscle Shoals resolution and specifically rejected permanent federal ownership and operation of the power and fertilizer business.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: When Japan occupied Manchuria, Hoover’s administration adopted a policy of refusing recognition to changes that violated treaty obligations.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Hoover reported that his administration instructed consuls to deny visas to prospective immigrants likely to become public charges, cutting monthly visa issuance from about 24,000 to about 7,000.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called for rigid enforcement and extension of federal regulation of utilities and competition law where states cannot act, while also wanting some regulation relaxed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Described the Republican party as ever a party of progress and urged a way forward rather than a return to the past.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Hoover rejected revolution as a way to solve the political and social problems facing the United States and urged institutional reform.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Said the world had been disillusioned by the divine right of kings and denied that divinity rests in any ruling class or person.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Called self-interest a necessary motive for production but said civilization cannot rest on unrestrained self-interest.

separated-powers.rationale: Said self-government requires decentralization and many checks and balances to safeguard liberty.

simple-living.rationale: Praised rising material standards and the spread of comforts as the base of civilization.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Hoover argued that reform should grow out of the country’s established institutions and rely on cooperative action within them.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Abhorred autocracy and held that officials may not choose which laws to enforce.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Described the Russian regime as socialism applied nationally and as having failed.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wrote that people do not live by bread alone and that spiritual forces must inspire the social and economic system.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described government as the umpire of the social system maintaining equality before the law, not a tool of one class.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Hoover created the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, authorizing federal credit directed to railroads, financial institutions and agricultural credit channels during the Depression.

state-harmful.rationale: Described government as an umpire and encourager of voluntary cooperation, supported public regulation, education and health services, and rejected the idea that the state is harmful in itself.

strong-leader.rationale: Hoover defended the independence of the Supreme Court and warned that subordinating the Court to the executive would undermine a constitutional safeguard.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Defended free speech, free press and assembly as the core of liberalism and warned bureaucracy erodes them.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Hoover approved the Tariff Act of 1930, which set protective duties on agricultural and manufactured imports.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hoover signed the Revenue Act of 1932, whose estate tax imposed rising marginal rates on larger estates.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hoover signed the Revenue Act of 1932, which imposed progressively higher income surtaxes as individual net income increased.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hoover signed the Revenue Act setting federal taxes on personal incomes, corporations and estates.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hoover began ending direct U.S. administration of Haiti, transferring responsibilities away from the American high commissioner and moving toward diplomatic relations through a minister.

total-state.rationale: Hoover argued that government control of everyday economic activity would extend to people’s thoughts and destroy free expression and representative institutions.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: Hoover drew down the Marine presence in Haiti and Nicaragua while retaining Marines to guard the U.S. legation in China.

unions-good.rationale: Hoover signed the Norris–LaGuardia Act, protecting workers’ freedom to organize and limiting federal injunctions against collective labor action.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Held that citizens who dislike a law must seek repeal and not violate it.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: Hoover rejected the old prediction that wages could never rise above subsistence, arguing that American industrial productivity had raised workers’ living standards and would continue to do so.

war-builds-character.rationale: Described war as destruction that leaves nations poorer and spiritually dislocated.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argued that property assembled in groups controlling the state makes capital an oppressor and that economic domination by a few must not be tolerated.

notes: This pass cross-checked the presidential speeches and annual messages against statutes and executive actions. Research covered federalism, the courts, law enforcement and reform, monetary policy, taxation, labor, agriculture, industrial policy and relief, diplomacy, armaments and immigration, conservation and technological change, and the social, cultural, religious and civil-liberties topics in the statement bank. The 1930 visa instructions are documented. They do not establish that Hoover personally directed the broader local campaigns to repatriate people of Mexican descent.
